courses.summary: MBBS is the Students Traffic catalogue category for undergraduate-entry medicine degrees. Texila American University Zambia maps its Bachelor of Medicine and Bachelor of Surgery (MBChB) programme to this category: a direct-entry, single-cycle five-year programme, with a one-year foundation stage (HPFP) required for applicants without qualifying A-Level science grades.

universities.name: Texila American University Zambia
universities.summary: Texila American University Zambia opened in 2016 and enrolled its first MBChB cohort in 2017. The programme is listed in the WHO World Directory of Medical Schools with ECFMG-certification eligibility for graduates from 2023 onward, is accredited by Zambia's Health Professions Council (HPCZ), and the university is registered with Zambia's Higher Education Authority as one of the country's multi-campus private higher-education institutions.
universities.campusLifestyle: The MBChB programme is a for-profit, private-university offering, part of the wider Texila American University group with campuses in several countries; Zambia-specific accreditation (HEA registration, HPCZ programme accreditation) is kept distinct in the university's own materials from its Guyana campus's separate accreditation. International (foreign) students receive a complimentary six-month hostel stay on enrollment.
universities.cityProfile: Lusaka is Zambia's capital and largest city, home to several major public hospitals used for the university's clinical training, including University Teaching Hospital and Levy Mwanawasa University Teaching Hospital. The city hosts a range of government ministries, regional diplomatic missions and other higher-education institutions, giving international medical students access to a reasonably sized urban support network alongside the university's own hostel and counselling services.
universities.practicalExposure: The five-year MBChB (following a one-year Health Professions Foundation Programme for applicants without qualifying A-Level grades) runs preclinical foundations in Years 1-2, with hospital-based clinical rotations across Years 3-5: Internal Medicine (30 weeks), General Surgery (30 weeks), Paediatrics (20 weeks), Obstetrics and Gynaecology (20 weeks), Psychiatry (10 weeks) and Community Medicine (10 weeks). Clinical training runs across a named hospital network: Chainama Hills Hospital (250 beds), University Teaching Hospital Adult and Children's sites (2,000+ and 350 beds respectively), Levy Mwanawasa University Teaching Hospital (1,000 beds), Cancer Disease Hospital (252 beds) and Maina Soko Military Hospital (260+ beds). Post-graduation internship is provided in a teaching hospital under consultant supervision. Graduates receive the MBChB degree.
universities.hostelOverview: International (foreign) students receive a complimentary six-month hostel stay on enrollment, in shared rooms (2- or 3-sharing) with a communal kitchen, study room, laundry and 24/7 security. No cost figure is published for accommodation beyond the initial six-month period; applicants should confirm current rates directly with Student Counsellors. The university does not provide accommodation for visiting family members.
universities.dietarySupport: Hostel accommodation includes a communal kitchen with a gas stove and fridge; there is no in-house cafeteria, and students self-cater. No specific food-cost figure is published.
universities.safetyOverview: Hostel facilities include a daytime caretaker and night security, with gender-specific accommodation. No wider university-published campus-safety statistics were found.
universities.studentSupport: Admissions and hostel queries are handled through the university's Student Counsellors and admissions office (enquiry@tau.edu.zm). The university's own materials state its MBChB curriculum was reviewed by South Africa's Health Professions Council in November 2024 and found to meet professional standards for registration purposes, subject to South Africa's own Medical Board Examination.

Programme-specific accreditation from Zambia's Health Professions Council (HPCZ), with the university itself registered with Zambia's Higher Education Authority.

thingsToConsider: ECFMG-certification eligibility applies only to graduates from 2023 onward, reflecting the programme's comparatively recent formal international-recognition track record.

Fees are non-refundable in most circumstances (application fee, admission charges, visa processing, seat deposit, and the current semester's fee once a semester has started); confirm the current refund policy in writing before paying.

The university's scholarship page describing an Academic Excellence Scholarship and a Kenneth Kaunda Scholarship was last confirmed available in December 2023 and may not reflect current terms; the Kenneth Kaunda Scholarship's naming and framing suggest a likely Zambia-national focus, though this is not explicitly stated.

faq.question: Is the MBChB programme direct-entry after high school?
faq.answer: Yes. Applicants with qualifying A-Level science grades (Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Mathematics, English at grade C or above) enter the 5-year MBChB directly. Applicants with O-level or equivalent results instead complete a 1-year Health Professions Foundation Programme first.

faq.question: What qualification is awarded on graduation?
faq.answer: Graduates receive the MBChB (Bachelor of Medicine, Bachelor of Surgery) degree.

faq.question: What entrance exam does the university require?
faq.answer: There is no standalone written entrance exam. Selection uses an online assessment test plus a personal interview assessing motivation, resilience and problem-solving.

faq.question: What is the current tuition fee?
faq.answer: For international students: USD 8,200 in Year 1, USD 4,500 in Year 2, and USD 5,500 in each of Years 3-5, for a five-year total of roughly USD 29,200, per the university's official tuition page. The one-year foundation programme (for O-level entrants) costs an additional USD 8,000.

faq.question: Are there additional fees besides tuition?
faq.answer: Yes -- an application fee, admission processing charge, visa processing charge and seat deposit are all referenced in the university's admissions materials, but exact amounts were not published; confirm these directly with admissions. Most fees are non-refundable.

faq.question: When does the academic year start and when can I apply?
faq.answer: The university runs two intakes a year, in March and September. The September 2026 intake is confirmed open, but no specific application deadline date is published -- confirm the current cutoff directly with admissions.

faq.question: Is a scholarship available for international Medicine students?
faq.answer: An Academic Excellence Scholarship offers merit-based tuition discounts (5-10%) for top-performing students, and a Kenneth Kaunda Scholarship offers a full tuition award for one MBChB student per year, though its framing suggests it may be focused on Zambian nationals. This information was last confirmed available in December 2023 and should be reverified for current terms.

faq.question: Do Indian students need NEET to join this programme?
faq.answer: The university's own admissions criteria do not reference NEET. Separately, India's National Medical Commission requires Indian citizens and OCI holders who obtain a primary medical qualification abroad to have qualified NEET-UG, whose result serves as the mandatory Eligibility Certificate.

programmes.officialTitle: Bachelor of Medicine and Bachelor of Surgery (MBChB)

fee.notes: Officially published international tuition, per the university's Tuition and Aid page: USD 8,200 (Year 1), USD 4,500 (Year 2), USD 5,500 (Years 3-5 each), for a 5-year total of approximately USD 29,200. Applicants entering via the 1-year Health Professions Foundation Programme (O-level route) pay an additional USD 8,000 for that foundation year. Application fee, admission processing charge, visa processing charge and seat deposit are referenced but not quantified in any source found. Most fees are non-refundable; a pre-semester-start withdrawal refunds tuition minus non-refundable charges, while a post-start withdrawal also forfeits the current semester's fee.

eligibleAudiences: International applicants with IGCSE A-Level results in Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Mathematics and English at grade C or above (direct MBChB entry), or O-level-equivalent results plus completion of the 1-year Health Professions Foundation Programme
restrictions: Selection uses an online assessment test and interview rather than a standardized entrance exam
English proficiency (for non-English-speaking-country applicants) requires TOEFL, IELTS 4.0 or above, or Cambridge/IB equivalents
Indian applicants must separately hold a current NEET-UG qualification under India's National Medical Commission rules; this is not administered by the university itself
audienceEligibility.notes: Country-specific O-level equivalents are explicitly recognized for South Africa, Namibia, Zimbabwe, Botswana, Malawi and Nigeria.

admissionsContent.overview: Applicants apply online, pay the application fee, submit academic documents, complete an online assessment test and interview, and progress through a multi-stage offer process (Eligibility Letter, Provisional Admission Letter, Admission Confirmation Letter, Final Admission Letter) tied to fee installment payments.

eligibility.intro: Admission requires qualifying secondary-education science results (direct A-Level entry, or O-level results plus the foundation programme), English proficiency, and a passing result on the university's online assessment and interview.
items: IGCSE A-Level in Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Mathematics and English (grade C or above) for direct entry, or O-level-equivalent results plus the 1-year Health Professions Foundation Programme
English proficiency: TOEFL, IELTS 4.0 or above, or Cambridge/IB equivalents, for non-English-speaking-country applicants
Online assessment test and personal interview assessing motivation, resilience and problem-solving
Indian applicants: current NEET-UG qualification per India's National Medical Commission rules, separate from the university's own admission process

applicationSteps: Complete the online application form via apply.tauedu.org and pay the application fee
Upload photograph, ID proof and academic credentials
Complete the online assessment test and interview
Receive an Eligibility Letter, e-sign the admission letter and pay the seat deposit
Complete document review, pay the first fee installment, and receive the Provisional and then Final Admission Letter before enrollment
